mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate directly reduces the risk-free rate, lowering equity discount rates and increasing present value of future cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 1.0% over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A high unemployment rate signals weak labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 4.5% over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts below 1200 thousand units signals weakening residential demand, which precedes economic slowdown and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when HOUST < 1200.0 over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production above 105.0 index points signals robust manufacturing activity, supporting corporate earnings growth and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO > 105.0 over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts above 1250 thousand units and retail sales above 490,000 million dollars indicate broad-based consumer demand strength, which typically results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction effect is not significant: average 20-day S&P 500 return when both conditions are met is not significantly higher than when only one condition is met (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL > 245.0) combined with accommodative monetary policy (FEDFUNDS < 1.2%) signals strong growth without immediate rate hikes, supporting equity valuations and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Average 20-day S&P 500 return during periods meeting both CPIAUCSL>245.0 and FEDFUNDS<1.2% is not significantly positive (mean <= 0) over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 4.5%), a rising unemployment rate signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE > 4.5% over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During manufacturing slowdown regimes (INDPRO < 100.0), a decline in industrial production signals weakening economic activity, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO < 100.0 over a 5-year rolling window.
